APPLICATION 05 / COLLECT

Keep the water surface clear, every day.

Choosing a surface-cleaning vessel depends on the water area, the type and volume of debris, shore facilities for docking and charging, and whether local rules allow unmanned operation.

Applications / Autonomous water-surface cleaning

Who this is for

Harbour and fishing-port operators, reservoir and water-utility managers, scenic-area and municipal waterway authorities.

Project inputs

  • Water area, shoreline and navigation traffic
  • Debris types and estimated daily volume
  • Launch, mooring, charging and unloading points
  • Local rules for unmanned vessels and radio equipment
Build a project brief
01

Start with debris volume and frequency

Estimate how much floating debris arrives, what it is made of and how often the surface must be cleared. Plastics, leaves, algae and oil films call for different collection and unloading arrangements.

02

Match the vessel to the water area

The S-Cleaner suits smaller and sheltered waters such as marinas, scenic lakes and reservoir inlets. The M-Cleaner, with a larger basket and hull, suits open harbours, coastal water within about 2 km of shore and large reservoirs.

03

Plan docking, charging and unloading

Each vessel needs a launch point, a mooring or docking station, charging and a place to empty the basket. Unloading trips reduce effective coverage, so plan them with the route.

04

Confirm permits, radio and supervision

Unmanned vessels depend on local waterway rules, radio certification for the remote link, insurance and a plan for manual takeover. Confirm these before purchase rather than after delivery.

05

Verify cleaning results

Agree how results will be measured: area covered, debris weight collected, operating hours and interventions. Ask for records from comparable sites and run an acceptance trial.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Questions worth resolving.

Can a cleaning vessel replace manual cleaning boats?

It can take over routine collection of light floating debris in suitable conditions. Heavy debris, storms and busy channels may still need crewed boats, so define the split of work.

Can these vessels handle oil spills?

The manufacturer describes oil-film collection for the M-Cleaner. Spill-response equipment is regulated in many jurisdictions, so treat oil collection as a separate requirement to confirm against local rules.
